title: Selective oral decontamination of the esophagus to reduce microbial burden among patients with esophageal cancer
summary:
In Germany, approximately 10 new cases of esophageal cancer per 100.000 inhabitants per year can be observed. Histologically, squamous cell carcinoma has to be distinguished from adenocarcinoma. Treatment is based on multimodal therapy. Dependent on histology and staging, neo-adjuvant chemo- or radio-chemotherapy will be applied followed by surgery. Esophageal resection with intrathoracic anastomosis (Ivor Lewis procedure) is the surgical treatment of choice. However, this operation is associated with high rates of postoperative mortality and morbidity. Infectious complications including pneumonia, anastomotic leakage with mediastinitis and pleural empyema, and surgical site infections are the most frequent reasons for prolonged hospitalization and death after surgery. Cancer patients with immunosuppression due to the underlying disease and eventual chemo- or radiotherapy are under an increased risk to develop infectious complications. 
It is well acknowledged that microbiota from the upper gastrointestinal tract are associated with infectious complications after esophagectomy. Selective decontamination of the digestive tract might alter esophageal microbiome resulting in decreased rates of postoperative complications. However, no randomised-controlled data are available to support this hypothesis. Therefore, the aim of this needed multi-centre trial is to compare selective oral decontamination (SOD) of the esophagus with a placebo in adult patients undergoing elective esophagectomy due to esophageal cancer. For the study, 164 patients will be randomly assigned to one of the two treatment arms. The study will last 24 months; it will take 18 months to enrol patients in the study.

interventions.name: Selective oral decontamination of the esophagus 7 days prior to operation, intraoperatively and 5 days postoperatively.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Patients ≥18 years
• Histologically confirmed esophageal squamous cell or adenocarcinoma
• Planned elective esophagectomy with intrathoracic anastomosis
Exclusion criteria:
• Patients <18 years
• Complete dysphagia with inability to orally ingest the study drug
• Known allergies or intolerances against the above-mentioned drugs
• Inability to provide informed consent.
